title: Reading a graduated syringe: scale intervals and where to read the plunger
blurb: Work out what each small mark on any syringe is worth, read the volume at the right edge of the plunger seal and type it in Pearson format.
question: A 5 mL syringe has a number at each whole mL and small marks every 0.2 mL. The plunger seal lines up with the third small mark above 2. What volume has been drawn up?

teach.h: Every syringe has its own scale
teach.body: Item 1 of every Part A practice paper shows a syringe and asks what volume has been drawn up. A graduation is one small marked step on the barrel; its value depends on the syringe. Plain English: never assume each small line is 0.1 mL. Work it out: take the gap between two numbered marks and divide by the number of small spaces between them.

head: Syringe
Numbers every
Small mark
teach.caption: These vary by manufacturer: always work the value out from the picture or the stem.

teach.body: Read the volume at the top edge of the rubber plunger seal: the ring nearest the needle or tip, where the liquid ends. The back ring of the seal and the end of the plunger rod are not the reading. Count small marks from the numbered mark just below that edge.

items: Staff nurse Chloe Williams draws up an oral dose in a 5 mL oral syringe. Numbers are at each whole mL, with 5 spaces between numbers.
The front edge of the seal is on the third small mark above 2.
Sense check: it sits just over halfway between 2 and 3, and she types 2.6 mL.

teach.h: Reading errors on a 5 mL syringe at 2.6 mL

teach.text: Misreading the graduations is the classic syringe error: a 5 mL syringe marked every 0.2 mL read as if every mark were 0.1 mL turns 2.6 mL into 2.3 mL. Count spaces, not lines, and start from the numbered mark below the seal.

items.label: 0.6 mL with no leading zero: marked wrong
trailing zero: not the accepted form

items: Value per small space = gap between numbers ÷ number of spaces.
Read at the front edge of the plunger seal.
Check the answer sits between the two numbers you can see.
Type the unit when asked: mL, with a leading zero below 1.

summary: You can now work out the value of each graduation on any syringe, read the volume at the front edge of the plunger seal, and enter the reading in Pearson format.

A.q: A 5 mL syringe has a number at each whole mL and small marks every 0.2 mL. The front edge of the plunger seal lines up with the fourth small mark above 1. What volume has been drawn up? Please use the correct unit.

whyNot.0: Counted each mark as 0.1 mL; they are 0.2 mL.
whyNot.1: Counted three spaces; the seal is on the fourth mark above 1.
whyNot.2: Counted five marks; the fifth mark would be the number 2.

A.q: A 1 mL syringe has a number at every 0.1 mL and small marks every 0.01 mL. The plunger seal lines up with the sixth small mark above 0.2. What volume has been drawn up? Please use the correct unit and write your answer to two decimal places.

whyNot.1: Counted each mark as 0.02 mL; they are 0.01 mL.
whyNot.2: Counted each mark as 0.1 mL; they are 0.01 mL.
whyNot.3: Counted five spaces; the seal is on the sixth mark.

A.q: A 10 mL syringe has a number at each whole mL and small marks every 0.5 mL. The plunger seal lines up with the first small mark above 6. What volume has been drawn up? Please use the correct unit and write your answer to one decimal place.

whyNot.0: Counted the mark as 0.1 mL; it is 0.5 mL.
whyNot.1: Counted the mark as 0.2 mL; it is 0.5 mL.
whyNot.3: Started from 7; the seal is one mark above 6.

B.q: A child's dose is drawn up in a 3 mL syringe with numbers every 0.5 mL and small marks every 0.1 mL. The seal lines up with the third small mark above 1.5. What volume has been drawn up? Please use the correct unit and write your answer to one decimal place.

whyNot.0: Counted each small mark as 0.5 mL; that is the gap between numbers.
whyNot.1: Counted each mark as 0.2 mL; they are 0.1 mL.
whyNot.3: Counted each mark as 0.01 mL; they are 0.1 mL.

B.q: A client's medicine is drawn up in a 2 mL syringe with numbers every 0.5 mL and small marks every 0.1 mL. The seal lines up with the second small mark below 1.5. What volume has been drawn up? Please use the correct unit and write your answer to one decimal place.

whyNot.1: Counted above 1.5; the seal is below it.
whyNot.2: Counted each mark as 0.2 mL; they are 0.1 mL.
whyNot.3: Counted each mark as 0.01 mL; they are 0.1 mL.

B.q: A 20 mL syringe has numbers every 5 mL and small marks every 1 mL. The seal lines up with the second small mark above 10. What volume has been drawn up? Please use the correct unit.

whyNot.0: Counted each mark as 0.1 mL; on this syringe they are 1 mL.
whyNot.1: Counted one space; the seal is on the second mark.
whyNot.2: Counted each mark as 5 mL; that is the gap between numbers.

C.q: A 10 mL syringe has a number at each whole mL with 5 equal small spaces between numbers. The seal lines up with the fourth small mark above 3. What volume has been drawn up? Please use the correct unit and write your answer to one decimal place.

whyNot.0: Assumed 0.1 mL per mark; 1 mL ÷ 5 spaces is 0.2 mL.
whyNot.2: Assumed 0.25 mL per mark; 5 spaces make 0.2 mL each.
whyNot.3: Counted three spaces; the seal is on the fourth mark.

C.q: A child is prescribed 0.35 mL. A 1 mL syringe has numbers every 0.1 mL and small marks every 0.01 mL. The seal is on the third small mark above 0.4. How much must be expelled to leave the dose? Please use the correct unit and write your answer to two decimal places.

whyNot.1: Read the seal as 0.4 mL; it is three marks above, at 0.43 mL.
whyNot.2: Read each mark as 0.1 mL (0.7 mL) before subtracting.

C.q: A client needs 2.4 mL from a 5 mL oral syringe with a number at each whole mL and small marks every 0.1 mL. How many small marks above 2 should the front edge of the seal reach?

whyNot.0: Counted 0.2 mL per mark; they are 0.1 mL.
whyNot.1: Counted from zero, not from the numbered mark 2.
whyNot.3: Counted 0.01 mL per mark; they are 0.1 mL.

reteach.title: Count the spaces, not the lines
reteach.question: Between the 1 and 2 on a syringe there are 4 small lines. What is each space worth?

blocks.body: Lines are like fence posts and spaces are the gaps. Four small lines between 1 and 2 make five spaces (the numbered lines are the end posts), so each space is 1 ÷ 5 = 0.2 mL. Count spaces upward from the numbered line below the seal.

head: Small lines between numbers
Spaces
Value if numbers are 1 mL apart

blocks.text: Read the front ring of the seal, nearest the tip, never the end of the plunger rod.

explain.body: Gap between numbered marks ÷ number of spaces.

test.q: A syringe has numbers at 0.5, 1, 1.5 and 2 mL, with 5 equal small spaces between each pair of numbers. What volume does each small space represent? Please use the correct unit.

whyNot.0: This is the gap between numbers, not one space.
whyNot.2: Divided 1 mL by 5; the numbers are 0.5 mL apart.

explain.h: Count up from the number below
explain.body: Volume = numbered mark below the seal + spaces counted x value per space.

test.q: A 2 mL syringe has numbers every 0.5 mL and small marks every 0.1 mL. The seal is on the fourth small mark above 0.5. What volume has been drawn up? Please use the correct unit and write your answer to one decimal place.

whyNot.0: Counted each mark as 0.01 mL; they are 0.1 mL.
whyNot.1: Counted two spaces; the seal is on the fourth mark.
whyNot.2: Counted each mark as 0.2 mL; they are 0.1 mL.

explain.body: The seal has two rings. Read the one nearest the tip: that is where the liquid ends.

test.q: The front ring of a plunger seal lines up with 2.4 mL and the back ring with 2.8 mL. What volume has been drawn up? Please use the correct unit.
test.why: The volume is read at the front ring, nearest the tip: 2.4 mL.

whyNot.0: This is the back ring; read the ring nearest the tip.
whyNot.1: Averaged the two rings; read the front ring.
whyNot.2: This is the width of the seal, not the volume.

explain.body: Leading zero below 1, no trailing zeros, unit as mL.

test.q: A syringe reading is seven tenths of a millilitre and the question asks you to use the correct unit. Which answer is in the correct format?
test.why: Leading zero, no trailing zero, unit mL: 0.7 mL.

whyNot.0: No leading zero: Pearson marked ".9 mL" wrong.
whyNot.2: The trailing zero is not the accepted form.
